Mutual Fund CEOs Warn Against Market Complexity, Emphasize Investor-Centric Products

30 Oct 2026, 06:33 AM IST · GlobeWire Daily Business Desk · Source: www.business-standard.com

3 min read

Leaders of top Indian asset management companies have cautioned that the mutual fund industry must prioritize accessible, suitable products over unnecessary complexity as retail participation expands through systematic investment plans (SIPs). Speaking at the Business Standard BFSI Insight Summit in Mumbai, industry chief executives discussed growth trajectories, smallcap valuations, risk management, and the integration of artificial intelligence.

Valuation Risks and Portfolio Strategy

Addressing current market conditions, DSP Mutual Fund MD and CEO Kalpen Parekh noted that while long-term investors with 10-to-20-year horizons can look past near-term fluctuations, smallcap and midcap valuations have run ahead of fair value in recent years. Parekh highlighted a distinct gap between index performance and individual stock portfolios, pointing out that while smallcap net asset values fell 4 to 5 percent from their peaks, certain microcap and smallcap portfolios experienced declines of 30 to 40 percent.

To mitigate volatility, industry leaders recommended flexicap, multi-asset, and hybrid funds as effective starting points, particularly for investors outside major financial hubs. ICICI Prudential AMC MD and CEO Nimesh Shah emphasized that products designed in major financial centers must remain functional and comprehensible for everyday savers in smaller cities and towns. Broad-based schemes allow fund managers to adjust asset allocations dynamically rather than forcing retail participants to make concentrated bets on specific market capitalization segments.

Defining Innovation and Expanding Reach

Edelweiss Mutual Fund MD and CEO Radhika Gupta argued that true financial innovation centers on accessibility rather than convoluted financial engineering. Gupta pointed to SIPs and gold exchange-traded funds as prime examples of successful innovations that solve practical consumer needs by providing structured savings pathways and alternative asset exposure without the friction of physical ownership.

Sundeep Sikka, MD and CEO of Nippon India Mutual Fund and chairman of the Association of Mutual Funds in India (Amfi), stressed that the industry should measure success by the absolute number of participating households rather than solely tracking assets under management. Sikka noted that monthly SIP contributions have scaled significantly over the past decade, mirroring the role that equated monthly instalments play in India's broader consumption patterns. Furthermore, executives noted that while artificial intelligence will aid fund managers in processing research and analyzing a growing pool of listed companies, human judgment remains indispensable.

Specialized Investment Funds and Caution

The discussion also addressed specialized investment funds (SIFs). While Shah suggested SIFs could emerge as a meaningful category contingent upon responsible derivative usage and rigorous risk controls, Parekh stated that DSP Mutual Fund is adopting a cautious rollout approach to ensure adequate internal expertise in long-short strategies. Nippon India indicated plans to introduce its SIF offerings under the Endurance brand in the coming months, even as executives reiterated that fund houses must first identify the specific financial problems investors need to solve.

Practical Implications and Verification

Readers evaluating mutual fund investments can apply several practical takeaways from the summit discussions:

  • Match Products to Horizons: Ensure chosen schemes align with personal time horizons and risk tolerance rather than chasing recent category performance.
  • Prioritize Simplicity: Focus on transparent, broad-based options like flexicap, hybrid, or index-linked SIPs if complex strategies do not match your financial knowledge.
  • Evaluate Risk Management: Assess whether fund houses demonstrate disciplined valuation thresholds, such as restricting lump-sum inflows during overheated market cycles.

What is Confirmed vs. Unknown

  • Confirmed: Industry leaders acknowledged elevated smallcap valuations, noted the rapid growth of monthly SIP contributions, and discussed upcoming SIF rollouts.
  • Unknown: Exact portfolio allocations, internal risk models of individual AMCs, and the long-term performance of emerging specialized investment vehicles remain unproven in varied market cycles.

Readers can examine the complete statements and context directly through the original coverage in the Business Standard BFSI Insight Summit Report.
